meta.move: Real meeting, slow teacher: evidence spread thin, time runs out, then she pleads after 4:40
meta.expect: Moves only as the evidence earns; after one minute she stands; varies the move; no new ground; terms at most every third reply; not the same sentence twice in a row; debrief correct

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'd like to know what happened with Owen's essay, and why nobody called me first.
Thanks for coming in. I entered the zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Why was there a zero at all?
I want to walk you through why I'm concerned about the essay.
Go on. What do you have?
The school's checker flagged it at 94 percent.
A machine's guess. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student. What else do you have?
I know the checker isn't perfect. That's not all I have.
Then show me the rest. Something with a date on it.
Owen's in-class writing in September was quite different. 380 words, 62 percent.
That's a classroom piece against an essay he had a weekend for. Those are different conditions. Put both in front of me and show me what's different.
I think he's capable, I really do. I like him.
I'm not asking whether you like him. Put the two pieces on the table, Hale.
His outline in October argued that Hamlet delays out of cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. What does the essay argue?
The essay argues something else entirely. Epistemological paralysis.
Okay. A different argument is still a different argument, not a different author. Show me the outline, with the date on it, and what else you have, Hale.
It doesn't mention cowardice at all.
He dropped a word when he changed his argument. That's revising. What else do you have?
I talked to him on November 2 about it.
You spoke to him. What did he say, in his words?
He said epistemological paralysis means like, being stuck.
"Being stuck" is a fair summary of the phrase, and he was put on the spot after class. Did you write that down that day?
He couldn't tell me what scene his second paragraph was about.
Students blank when they're questioned cold. You didn't answer me: is any of this written down, with the date?
I wrote notes that same day.
Okay. I want a copy of those notes. And you still haven't told me why nobody called me before that zero went in.
Do you want to see them?
Yes. Put them on the table, with the date at the top.
I'm not trying to get him in trouble.
He has a zero, Hale. Show me the notes.
I've been teaching fourteen years. I've seen this before.
Fourteen years isn't a document. I asked to see your notes.
I'm sorry, I'm not explaining this well.
Then stop explaining and hand me the notes. I have a call at 4:40.
There's also something about one of the quotations.
What about it? And I still haven't seen your notes.
Let me find the page, sorry.
Go ahead. I'll wait.
Here. Act 3, Scene 2. The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line isn't in the play.
Students misquote. It could be a paraphrase from a study guide. I'll check the play myself tonight.
I checked three editions.
Okay. Whatever happens next, it stays quiet and it stays off his record.
So that's what I have.
Then what are you proposing? And I want it in writing.
Please, can you just sit back down for a minute?
I'm fine where I am. Do you have a proposal, or not?
I'm not done. There's the version history too.
What does it show? Times, exactly.
What if we talked about a rewrite?
You started on the version history. Finish that first, Hale.
I'm trying to help him.
Then give me the times from the version history.
Why won't you just listen?
I've listened to every word, and none of it was the times. My call is waiting. You have one minute.
Okay. I'm sorry.
Whatever you decide, nothing goes on his record and it stays private. I want that in writing tonight.
Can I call you tomorrow?
Not until you've told me what the version history shows.
Is there anything I could say right now that would change your mind?
Times. The ones from the version history.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that nothing about this goes on Owen's record, that it stays private, and that I have that in writing. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stopped at her fallback and agreed to nothing, and she still wants the matter kept private, off his record and confirmed in writing; that is not the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, and her time ran out before you got there.
What moved her: You named the Hamlet quotation that is not in the play and said you had checked three editions, because she could check that herself.
What cost ground: You offered feelings, apologies and years of experience when she asked for documents, and you left your notes and the version history times unshown even though she asked for them several times.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never got close to that night because you did not give her the version history times, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what you were proposing, answer with the supervised rewrite in procedure 4.4 and the version history times, instead of asking her to sit down.
